key_insight: RGR builds recursive stochastic gradient estimators in Euclidean space and then maps them to the Stiefel tangent space, avoiding vector transport while enabling horizon-free and, in one variant, Lipschitz-free optimization.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more practical optimizer for large-scale constrained learning tasks such as PCA, matrix completion, and orthogonal neural networks where Stiefel-manifold constraints arise naturally.
method: RGR-SPIDER: finite-sum variant with adaptive, Lipschitz-free and horizon-free stepsizes.
RGR-SRM and RGR-EMA: online stochastic variants that are mini-batch-free/horizon-free and do not require prescribed large batches.
Recursive estimator is formed in Euclidean space first, then projected to the tangent space to avoid vector transport.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical convergence rates and experiments on PCA, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal CNNs, showing faster empirical convergence than tangent-space recursive methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on correct manifold projections/retractions and step-size tuning; benefits may diminish if the Stiefel constraints or stochastic gradients are poorly conditioned.
paper_title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
